correctness.rationale: The recurrence puts total weight δ^{d(i,j)}/(n−1) in row i for each target j≠i, distributed over its allowed first hops. The cycle has identical row sums by distance counts, with two vertices at each distance below n/2 and one antipode for even n. The common row sum is both an eigenvalue and the nonnegative matrix row-norm bound. On the star the center averages the leaves with total weight δ, and each leaf updates solely from the center with coefficient [δ+(n−2)δ²]/(n−1). Reduction to the center coordinate and common leaf coordinate gives the two nonzero eigenvalues ±ρ_S as claimed. Independently, let F=(n−1)ρ_C/δ, and P=(n−1)(1+(n−2)δ)−F², with the sign of ρ_S²−ρ_C². For n=3 and 4 this is 2δ−2 and −(1−δ)² respectively. For every n≥5, F is a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, F(0)=2, F′>0 on [0,1], and F(1)=n−1. Thus (F²)″=2(F′)²+2FF″>0, so P is strictly concave, P(0)=n−5≥0 and P(1)=0. This gives P>0 on the whole open interval, including n=5. The verification notes are consistent; the comparison is spectral, not an ordering of finite-time paths, and eigenvalues of opposite sign on bipartite graphs cause no problem for the spectral radius.
